description: Oilcan 1 on channel 1 plays eight drum hits per bar for four bars at 90 BPM, all at velocity 48. In every bar the hits fall on steps 1 (MIDI 36), 4 (38), 5 (37), 7 (38), 9 (36), 12 (38), 13 (37) and 15 (38). Oilcan is a drum voice: each MIDI note number picks a different pad of its default kit, so 36, 37 and 38 are three different drum sounds, here called timbres, played one after another on a single channel. Listen for the pad on MIDI 36 on beats 1 and 3, the pad on 37 on beats 2 and 4 and the pad on 38 filling the gaps. Every hit has the same velocity. Next, try muting the 38 hits by clearing their trigs and hear how the other two pads carry the pocket. Build it with the Separate fixed percussion example recipe.
synchronization: Observed framebuffer/grid sampled against host monotonic recording time; not sample-exact or physical-norns calibration.
title: Three sounds, one pocket
